title: Capacity onramp priority flow and GPU families mapping
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem statement: Enterprise customers are submitting dedicated capacity requests with inconsistent specification of SLA targets, unclear GPU family preferences, and mismatched scaling policies. This leads to long intake cycles, repeated follow-ups, incorrect capacity allocation (overprovisioning or underprovisioning), and manual adjustments by the capacity team. Goal: Create a clear onramp priority flow and a GPU-family → throughput mapping that PMs, sales engineers, and capacity ops can use during intake to produce a first-pass recommended capacity plan within 48 hours. Scope: non-bug intake flow for dedicated pools only (hosted Dedicated product). Excludes pricing negotiations and legal contract terms which will be handled by Sales. Deliverables: 1) a prioritized intake checklist (core questions and decision thresholds), 2) a GPU family mapping table with recommended reserved throughput bands and burst policies by workload archetype, 3) an escalation & canary rollout checklist for customers who need aggressive latency SLOs, and 4) an intake SLAs decision log template to attach to customer onboarding tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Checklist accepted by Capacity Ops and Solutions Engineering and published in Confluence
GPU-family mapping covers at least 3 common families (A100/H100/GPU-x) with recommended reserved throughput bands and expected p95 latencies for standard prompt sizes
Intake flow reduces follow-up clarification questions by 40% on pilot customers
First-pass recommended capacity plan generated within 48 hours for pilot customers following the checklist
Escalation/canary checklist tested in one pilot rollout with post-rollout notes captured
notes: Decision heuristics prioritized: customer p95 latency target -> model family compatibility -> token/sec throughput -> KV cache hit rate -> burst tolerance -> regional constraints
We will prefer GPU families with validated kernel coverage for our runtime (e.g., H100 for float16/quantized LLMs) when p95 latency < 300ms is required for typical prompt lengths
Reserved throughput bands are nominal (e.g., 50k, 200k, 800k tokens/min) and will be expressed alongside expected steady-state instance counts and typical autoscaling buffer
Burst policy recommendation: small customers -> no burst; growth customers -> burst credits with 10–20% short-term tolerance; enterprise customers -> guaranteed burst pool with pre-negotiated credits

Trade-offs: recommending higher-class GPUs (H100) reduces node count and can reduce latency variability, but increases committed cost. Include cost delta examples per 100k reserved tokens/min to help negotiation
We will not hardcode pricing; the mapping contains relative guidance (low/medium/high cost tier) and exact pricing will be attached from Sales pricing sheet
